_about: Newest results for pages/holdouts/recent.html, newest first. Add an entry when a PR changes what is known; build_pages.py writes the page. kind: halts, bound, structure, family or method. rests: coq, lean, computation, judgement or notes. machines: full TNF names; tag: a nickname shown with them.

entries.title: Pascal-crossing pair: the tail is not safe by itself
entries.text: For 1RB0LF_0LC0RE_0RA1LD_1LB0LD_0RA1RC_1LA--- and its twin 1RB0RA_0RC0LE_0LD1RA_1LB0RF_0LD1LC_1RD---, the reset map is proved for the head of the tape, and a halt can only come from a carry into the tail. Runs of the real machine with the countdown replaced at each reset, and the tail kept, show that irregular phase lengths can make it halt: 21 of 200 runs with X random in [36, 400], 25 of 100 with X in [2000, 4000]. Constant X, fixed growth ratios and 400 single changes to the true orbit never halted. So what keeps the true run alive is the way the 3/2 orbit's phase lengths shape the tail.

entries.title: Word-and-counter family: all six machines reduced to one macro map each
entries.text: The five sisters of 1RB0RF_1LC1RE_0LD0LC_1RD0RB_1RA0RB_0LC--- now have a complete macro map in Lean, as that machine had: the proved closed forms where they apply, and elsewhere a cell-by-cell simulation of the irregular stretch whose result Lean checks against the tape. For each, Lean proves that if the map never fails from step 27 the machine never halts. The maps do not fail in 10<sup>7</sup> steps (compiled evaluation) nor at any of 300 anomalies and collisions of the accelerated run. What is left is the same for all six: show that the map never fails.

entries.title: Pascal-crossing pair: the exact 3/2 reset map, in Lean for the head of the tape
entries.text: For 1RB0LF_0LC0RE_0RA1LD_1LB0LD_0RA1RC_1LA--- and its twin 1RB0RA_0RC0LE_0LD1RA_1LB0RF_0LD1LC_1RD---, Lean proves that a reset with X ≥ 36 is followed by the reset with X' = ⌊3X/2⌋ + 1 (X even) or + 3 (X odd), whatever the tail holds, as long as each excursion of the head into the tail comes back with the signature seen in simulation. Both machines reach a first reset from blank (X = 40 and X = 52), so their non-halting now rests only on the tail returning every phase.

entries.title: Rule-102 machine: which gaps a jump can make dangerous, in Lean
entries.text: For 1RB1LB_1LC0RD_0LE1LA_0RF1RA_1LE0LA_---0RB, Lean proves that the run of ys at the next jump is set by one series: after a jump of length L, the rest C of the gap must agree with mask L (word k is y iff k and L share no binary 1), and the run is the agreement minus one. So the danger pattern at the next jump needs exactly one gap per jump length, and under shielded sweeps exactly the rows of Pascal's triangle mod 2 (now proved, with the period 2b). The rule holds at all 10 jumps of the real run. The closest call had C equal to the mask on every old word, and was saved by words entering at the wall, which is what a proof must still control.

entries.title: Rule-102 machine: the 10 defect's jump and its clock, in Lean
entries.text: For 1RB1LB_1LC0RD_0LE1LA_0RF1RA_1LE0LA_---0RB, Lean proves both deep sweeps at a 10 defect for every length: with x in front the whole line is one row of rule 102, with y in front the defect jumps to the last slot of the gap's first x block, and after a jump over m slots the next jump comes exactly m sweeps later. So a defect's life is one map on its gap polynomial, F(W) = (1 + z)L C, and the danger pattern is a jump with nothing to land on. Every deep sweep of the real run to 1.2·107 steps follows it. The map alone does not prevent a halt, so the proof still needs the births.

entries.title: Outside proofs of busycoq PRs 43 to 68 compiled: 32 more machines decided
entries.text: Every machine proof in busycoq pull requests 43 to 68 compiles on busycoq's BB6 branch with Coq 8.20.1, and an audit file restates each one on busycoq's own halts and the exact table from our list. Of the 32 machines that were still open here, 6 halt and 26 never halt (the ledger names the authors: Alk, Dennis Koshta, Thomas Reus and DeepMind's Alex Havrilla). PR 60's two halting proofs need about 555 core-hours of jobs; their frameworks and four sample jobs pass here, and the machines stay open until the full runs are done.

entries.title: XOR machine: one round trip is rule 102 for every length, and a gap is dangerous only if it is a row of Pascal's triangle
entries.text: Lean proves that one right sweep and one left sweep replace every word of the left string (x = 111, y = 110) by the XOR of it and its right neighbour, for every string, and gives many sweeps in closed form by Lucas' theorem. A halt needs a gap after a 10 defect that turns all y; over GF(2) that happens exactly when the gap already is a row of Pascal's triangle mod 2 (checked for every gap up to 14 words, algebra not in Lean). The question is now which gaps the right end hands to a new defect.

entries.title: Running-parity machine: one bounce is one row of Pascal's triangle mod 2, solved by Lucas' theorem
entries.text: Lean proves that one bounce of the head maps the zone, a word in the 4-cell letters 1110 and 1111, to the running XOR of the word with a 1 appended, for every word, and gives the zone after j bounces in closed form by Lucas' theorem. It also proves that a right turn at a frozen block of odd length halts whatever the zone, so halting depends only on frozen-block parities. In 10<sup>10</sup> steps the tape right of every right turn is a word in the 2-cell letters 11 and 01, which rules that out; that invariant is observed, not proved. The same Lean holds, renamed, for a second machine with the same table.

entries.title: Hour-long accelerated runs of the 88 deeper machines: no halt, 81 bounds raised
entries.text: Each machine that an earlier screen found running past its recorded bound ran for an hour on the region-memo accelerator, an exact run-length simulator that reuses the macro of each stretch of tape. None halted. The new runs beat the 600-second ones in 82 cases, for example from 10<sup>149124</sup> to 10<sup>324388</sup> steps, and 81 ledgers now carry the higher bound.

entries.title: The irregular-tape holdout halts only if a chaotic word eats the whole run
entries.text: Next to its run of 1s this machine keeps a short word W that changes like a small chaotic engine rather than a counter. Lean proves the machine halts exactly when W eats the whole run of 1s. An exact run of 3·10<sup>9</sup> visits (8.6·10<sup>18</sup> steps) never saw W eat more than 18 cells in one visit. A proof would need a bound on one visit's bite that holds for every word the engine can produce, and none is in sight.

entries.title: The collapse pair: an exact cycle law, and no halt to 6.1·10<sup>135</sup> steps
entries.text: These two machines are the same nested ternary counter: the tape is a list of segments of 111-blocks drained by 3<sup>j</sup> per event, and segments run out one after another (collapses). After each collapse the counter settles into a new regime of the same kind. All 71 cycles observed follow one exact law (the oldest segment loses 2, the j-th loses 3<sup>j</sup>, the steps grow ninefold), and the next two collapses were run ahead of time without a halt. A Lean proof needs a new invariant first, because sweeps at the far end keep adding rules.

entries.title: The 554 undecided machines regrouped into ranked families
entries.text: Every pair of holdouts was compared by table distance, up to renaming and mirror image, and machines with the same mechanism were joined into families R01 to R15, ranked by how many machines one technique would settle. The families overview shows each family, what is known, the technique and the odds.

entries.title: Lean no-halt bounds for five counter machines
entries.text: For three marker counters on the F05 core, a base-5 counter and a binary counter, Lean proves the macro rules that the run-length simulator uses. Their runs to between 10<sup>100</sup> and 10<sup>1000</sup> steps are now proved no-halt bounds rather than observations.

entries.title: The near-miss holdout: a halting engine with its halt moved
entries.text: This is the table of DeepMind's busycoq pull request 93 with its halt removed and a detour halt added. Lean proves a halt needs state B reading 0 with 0, 0, 1 on its left. A Coq proof is ready except for the final engine run, which has not stopped in 10<sup>1336</sup> steps: the sibling's halting point comes round again on every lap and is survived each time.

entries.title: Two more starts of the T4 table halt (Coq)
entries.text: DeepMind's PR 93 engine, retargeted to the T4 table, reaches a halt from start D after 688,228 engine steps (tape about 2<sup>6326</sup> cells), and from start A of a table that runs like T4 after 350,227 engine steps. T4 now halts from all four starts. busycoq PR 102, an outside proof of the first, was also compiled here.

entries.title: busycoq PR 100 compiled here: another T4 start halts
entries.text: An outside Rocq proof runs this repository's Coq port of the PR 93 engine from the reflected, renamed C start to the halt (427,055 engine steps, tape about 2<sup>4360</sup> cells). It compiled here in 15,528 seconds.

entries.title: Region-memo no-halt bounds for 85 holdouts across seven families
entries.text: The first accelerated runs of the counter families, each checked cell for cell against a direct run up to 2·10<sup>9</sup> steps. No run halted, and each bound is recorded in the machine's ledger.

entries.title: How the 17 to 19 November proofs work, and four attempts to reuse them
entries.text: A write-up of the methods behind the week's outside proofs, with four attempts to carry them over to other holdouts.

entries.title: 32 recently decided holdouts explained
entries.text: Each machine decided by busycoq PRs 78 to 97 and 103 to 109 (DeepMind's proofs and this project's T4-engine proofs) now leads its explainer with the result and a plain-language section on how the proof works.

entries.title: The vampire family: seven holdouts, one explicit map
entries.text: Seven holdouts are one core table with a single entry varied. Lean proves that each halts from blank tape exactly when one map on (context, n) reaches a halting entry, and the map ran 2<sup>18</sup> passes without a halt.
